pedia: A military parade is a formation of soldiers whose movement is restricted. The American usage is "formation or military review". The military parade is now mostly ceremonial, though soldiers from time immemorial up until the late 19th century fought in formation.
strategy: Parade Grounds are an excellant way to remind your population of your military might, and educate your troops; but citizen's anger over ongoing war's may use the Parade Grounds as a focus for their anger.

name: Marco Polo's Embassy
pedia: Marco Polo was a trader, writer, and world traveler who lived in the late 13th and early 14th centuries. Starting as a young boy, he began traveling with his father and uncle, who were merchants and traders in Venice, along a route that would take him throughout Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. Throughout his life, he visited many places, bringing back detailed information concerning lands that no European before him had visited. Polo's book, "The Travels of Marco Polo", was the only source of reliable information on such exotic locales as Siam, Japan, Java, Tibet, and India that existed in Medieval Europe.
strategy: {color:building_text}Marco Polo's Embassy{/color} gives you three free trade routes and all merchant specialists give +1 gold.

name: Market
pedia: As cities grew and prospered, trade between the farmers, artisans, and craftsmen who lived in the vicinity contributed to the economic health of the city. It soon became apparent that the best way for conducting trade within the city was to have a central location, or marketplace, where the people offering goods and services, or seeking them, could meet and conduct business. As a city's marketplace grew larger and more active, the economic vitality of the city grew as well.
strategy: {color:building_text}Markets{/color} increase a city's wealth. They also increase the city's happiness with access to {color:highlight_text}Fur{/color}, {color:highlight_text}Ivory{/color}, {color:highlight_text}Silk{/color}, or {color:highlight_text}Whales{/color}.

name: Matter Decompiler
Mausoleum of Maussollos
pedia: Maussollos died in 349 BC. King of Caria during his lifetime, Maussollos wished to leave a reminder of himself for future generations in the form of a great tomb. In addition to hiring hundreds of laborers, Maussollos commissioned five of the finest artisans in the Hellenic world to design the hundreds of statues that were to line the peripheries of his white marble resting place.[PARAGRAPH:1]Over 130 feet tall upon completion, the Mausoleum of Maussollos stood by the harbor of Halicarnassus until 1522, when the Knights Hospitaller tore it down in order to use the stones to build defenses against the approaching Turks.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Mausoleum of Maussollos{/color} increases its builder's Golden Ages by fifty percent. It also increases the chances of a {color:unit_text}Great Artist{/color} appearing.

name: Ball Court
pedia: The Mesoamerican "Ball Game" (no native name has ever surfaced for the sport) originated in Southern Mexico, roughly two thousand years before the Common Era. By the time of the arrival of the Spanish, the game had become popular throughout Mexico, Guatemala and Belize, drawing crowds from both the upper echelons of society and the masses.[PARAGRAPH:1]While much of the game is still not understood, what is known is that two teams of two to four players each took to the field with the goal of keeping a small, rubber ball in the air by bouncing it off arms, hips and thighs. How the winner was decided is not known, but we do know that the losers often became the next sacrifice to the gods.[PARAGRAPH:1]The Ball Court held a deep religious significance for the Maya. Mayan Kings would often reenact a famous game between the God of the Underworld and the Heroes from the Popol Vuh, a Mayan sacred text. The King's victory on the Ball Court was said to be an omen of the continued survival of his city.
strategy: Build the {color:building_text}Ball Court{/color}, the Mayan replacement for the {color:building_text}Colosseum{/color}, to provide cities with three happiness instead of one.

name: Mech Assembly Plant
strategy: Mech Assembly Plant is required in city before you can build Mech units.

name: Organ Bank
Tavern
strategy: The {color:building_text}Tavern{/color} provides a small amount of Commerce and a Merchant slot.

name: Meeting of Minds
pedia: The Meeting of Minds is the ultimate expression of mind uploading technology; a single facility devoted to housing the greatest minds of a civilization, allowing them to communicate and collaborate. The result is an outpouring of artistic, philosophical, and scientific thought.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Meeting of Minds{/color} provides you with one free specialist of every type.

name: Menagerie
pedia: A menagerie is a name given to any collection of captive animals intended for display. Most menageries were kept for a royal or noble court as a symbol of power of wealth. Excavations in Egypt revealed a menagerie dated to circa 3500 BCE.
strategy: A {color:building_text}Menagerie{/color} provides Happiness and Culture. It requires a {color:unit_text}Captured Animal{/color} to build.

name: Mercenary Camp
pedia: Mercenaries have typically been drawn from those of low social status. As mercenaries traveled wherever soldiers were needed, they would typically set up encampments. These encampments were notorious as breeding grounds for violent behavior, as well as diseases brought from far places and exacerbated by poor sanitation.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Mercenary Camp{/color} provides a small amount of gold to offset the cost of your mercenary units, at the cost of some happiness and health.

name: Temple of Tlaloc
pedia: In Civilization IV, a religious pyramid is defined as an especially large and ornate religious building where the faithful worship. Only the most prosperous cities can afford to create pyramids, as they require huge amounts of raw material and years of dedicated labor by skilled craftsmen.
strategy: It requires its religion to be state religion to be built, unless you are running Free Church or Secular.

name: Pyramid of the Magician
pedia: The Pyramid of the Magician is a Mesoamerican step pyramid located in the ancient, Pre-Columbian city of Uxmal, Mexico. The structure is also referred to as the Pyramid of the Dwarf, Casa el Adivino, and the Pyramid of the Soothsayer. The pyramid is the tallest and most recognizable structure in Uxmal.

name: Calmacec
strategy: It requires its religion to be state religion to be built, unless you are running Free Church or Secular.

name: Teotihuacan
pedia: The Aztecs believed Teotihuacan was where the Sun had been created and that the city was built by the gods.

name: Temple of Quetzalcoatl
pedia: In Civilization IV, a temple is defined as a building where the faithful come to worship. Christians call their temples "churches," while Muslims call theirs "mosques," and Jews call theirs, simply, "temples." Temples are far more common than cathedrals, but much less large and ornate. Even the smallest village can possess a temple.
strategy: {color:building_text}Temples{/color} increase a city's happiness and culture. They are especially useful for expanding your civilization's borders during the early game. Temples don't require state religion to be built.

name: Metropolitan Administration
strategy: Build Village Halls, Town Halls and City Councils to add free specialist in your cities.

name: Laboratory
pedia: Historically, libraries and universities have acted as the primary centers of research for new ideas and technologies. The growth of private industry in the Modern Age has also given birth to hundreds of privately owned research facilities. These private laboratories, usually dedicated to research in a single field related to their founding company, have made tremendous advances in many fields including physics, biology, chemistry, and medicine. The growth of privately-funded research has vastly increased the speed at which mankind achieves new advances in science and technology.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Laboratory{/color} replaces the {color:building_text}Alchemist's Lab{/color} and increases your Science.

name: Military Academy
pedia: A "military academy" is an educational institution created to prepare young men and women for positions of leadership within the military. Such academies have existed throughout history.  At these institutions students are taught how to command troops, how to communicate effectively, how to read maps, how to give and receive orders. They learn of the history of warfare. They are taught to understand strategy and tactics, as well as engineering, logistics and intelligence, and they often study classic treatises such as Sun Tzu's "The Art of War." They learn how to operate the weapons of the day - whether muzzle-loading rifle or satellite-guided artillery. [PARAGRAPH:2]In most such institutions the young officers are taught a "code of honor" which emphasizes following orders and selfless dedication to their fellow soldiers and to their country. Students usually must follow an extremely rigorous course of physical training to ensure that their bodies are as finely-tuned as their minds. Military academies are undoubtedly effective, and most of the best generals of modern history have emerged from such institutions. [PARAGRAPH:2]President Thomas Jefferson created the United State's Military Academy at West Point in 1802. Its mission is: "To educate, train, and inspire the Corps of Cadets so that each graduate is a commissioned leader of character committed to the values of Duty, Honor, Country and prepared for a career of professional excellence and service to the Nation as an officer in the United States Army." [PARAGRAPH:2]
strategy: The {color:building_text}Military Academy{/color} increases a city's military unit production speed by half.

name: Military Airbase
pedia: An airbase (sometimes referred to as an airfield, military airport, or Air Force Station) is a military base that provides basing and support of military aircraft. They are different to civilian airports in that they do not provide for large volume of passenger transits, and cargo handling is not processed by the customs and immigration facilities. Some military air forces combine use of civilian airports with the hosting of military units. However, military aircraft usually use substantially different support equipment, and require facilities sufficiently isolated from civilian operations due to issues of aviation safety involving the weapon ordnance they use. [PARAGRAPH:2]While some airbases provide facilities very like civilian airports, for example RAF Brize Norton in Oxfordshire, England which has a terminal which caters for passengers for the Royal Air Force's scheduled flights, e.g., the TriStar to the Falkland Islands, most do not. Most military airbases are located remotely from populated areas due to the ever-present potential of in-flight accidents that may cause a crash and significant infliction of damage and casualties on civilian population.[PARAGRAPH:2]However, due to growth of urban centres, many military bases built during the Second World War are now located on the outskirts of large cities, and lack of required remoteness has cause constraints on flight operations to be introduced due to the noise pollution generated by the operation of military aircraft, such as night flying restrictions.[PARAGRAPH:2]The airbase operation is generally organised around its operational areas divided into the air command operations, air traffic control operations which are either towered or non-towered based, runways, taxiways, and ramps used in military operations to dislocate troops to be airlifted, or to stockpile cargo for loading. Refuelling is conducted in the pre-flight and inspection area.[PARAGRAPH:2]More substantial maintenance and repair is conducted in the squadron maintenance operations, usually in or close to their squadron hangars which are usually Hardened Aircraft Shelters to protect individual aircraft from aerial strikes. Maintenance is also carried out in the intermediate maintenance operations or the depot maintenance operations areas, the latter usually concerned with more substantial structural work such as changing an engine, crash repair, or field upgrades. A large part of the airbase surface is devoted to the maneuvering area used by aircraft to move around the different areas as they return from an air mission or prepare for one.[PARAGRAPH:2]Military flight operations often require a higher level of airbase security, and in recent years, many countries have adopted higher levels of security due to threats of terrorist attacks. This security in wartime is augmented by basing of air defence systems and their units, usually on the periphery of the airbase, which use anti-aircraft weapons such as surface-to-air missiles and their fire control radars, to protect from air attack. Other units located at the military airbase may be runway repair troops.
strategy: Increases the amount of air units city can hold and new air units will be more experienced. Slightly also increases defense against air attacks.

name: Military Base
pedia: A military base is any facility directly owned and operated by a military for its own purposes, mostly the accommodation and training of units. Bases became the primary centers of military force with the development of globe-spanning empires and modern warfare that required great amounts of supplies and logistics. Some bases rival small cities in their size and population.
strategy: Build a {color:building_text}Military Base{/color} to increase the production and experience of your units.

name: Mill
pedia: In general, a "mill" is any device used to break solid materials into small parts. The most common mill is a grist mill, used to grind grain into flour for baking. Gristmills have been known since before the Common Era, powered by water, wind, or human or animal power. Some form of energy was needed to be converted by machinery to power the grinding mechanism. By the Middle Ages, England had about one water-powered mill for every 300 inhabitants and nearly every village or town had its own mill.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Mill{/color} provides additional food and requires {color:highlight_text}Corn{/color}, {color:highlight_text}Rice{/color}, or {color:highlight_text}Wheat{/color} to build.

name: Mind-Control Center
pedia: As populations continue to grow, pushing human stress and unhappiness to unacceptably high levels, some cities are turning to mind-control centers to help alleviate the problem. Popularly known as "fun zones," these buildings broadcast a constant stream of soothing and enjoyable light entertainment which can be experienced by any human in the city equipped with a neural receiver (colloquially known as a "brain-jack"). [PARAGRAPH:1]While a "jacked-in" subject's productivity, creativity and intellect are somewhat impaired. However, the person is virtually incapable of being unhappy, no matter what the circumstances - so long as the constant barrage of meaningless entertainment is poured into their otherwise vacant brains. [PARAGRAPH:1]Despite its benefits, constructing a mind control center is not to be undertaken lightly: the broadcasts have been found to be nearly 100% addictive, and cutting an addict off from them may cause massive mental trauma ranging from catatonia to deep depression to homicidal rage. In other words, once a city's population is jacked in, there's no turning back - and a city had better have plenty of backups in case of broadcast equipment failure.
strategy: {color:building_text}Mind-Control Centers{/color} remove all {color:highlight_text}Unhappiness{/color} in a city, but they reduce the city's {color:highlight_text}Production{/color} by -25%.

name: Mind Storage
pedia: Mind uploading or whole brain emulation is the process of scanning and mapping a biological brain in detail and copying its state into a computer system or another computational device. The computer runs a simulation model so faithful to the original that it will behave in essentially the same way as the original brain, or for all practical purposes, indistinguishably.[PARAGRAPH:2]Mind storage provides the required computer power and mind databases for those citizes who decide to continue their lives in virtual realities. This grants a sort of immortality for those living in these virtual environments as long as the Mind Storage remains functional.
strategy: Mind Storage increases all your cities size by 1.

name: Mining Inc. Survey
pedia: For much of human history, victory has gone to those with access to the finest metals. From the Bronze Age onwards, metal tools, weapons and alloys have been an inherent part of the rise of civilization, spurring conquests and construction by the world's greatest empires. And while metal mining has had an impressive history, it was not until the nineteenth century that industrial mining truly began to take root.[PARAGRAPH:1]Two reasons explain this sudden intensification in mining operations. The first was the almost daily revolutions in the production of tools and consumer items, requiring a continual source of metal to produce them. The second was that the fuel that powered the Industrial Revolution was coal, nestled deep within the earth. In modern times, enormous excavators like the Bagger 288 have it possible to mine a pit three-hundred feet long and one-hundred feet deep in a day, a feat that, in the past, would have required the mobilization of nations.
strategy: Increases production and commerce if the resources needed by the Mining Inc. corporation are present in the city.

name: Missile Lab
pedia:
A missile silo is an underground, vertical cylindrical container for the storage and launching of intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs). They typically have the missile some distance under the surface, protected by a large "blast door" on top.
Until the 1960s ICBMs had been launched from surface bases. The Soviet Union used completely aboveground launchers similar to those found at a spaceport, which made them vulnerable to US bomber attack. The missile silo was first suggested in the 1950s in the United Kingdom as a suitable housing for Blue Streak missiles. Only one test missile silo was built in the UK at RAF Spadeadam and with the cancellation of the Blue Streak project, the UK ICBM nuclear missile capability was transferred in 1960 to submarines; however the idea of the underground rocket bunker was adopted by the USA.
strategy: Missile Labs allow for much faster production of nuclear and nonnuclear missiles.

name: Moai Statues
pedia: The Moai Statues are the most recognizable feature of Easter Island. Nine-hundred of these massive stone heads populate the island, most weighing up to 14 tons, with some reaching 82 tons and stretching forty feet into the sky.[PARAGRAPH:1]Theory holds that the Moai Statues were erected by the denizens of Easter Island around 1000 AD, the workers carving them at the Rano Raraku Quarry and transporting them to every corner of the island. The statues were dedicated to the various ancestors of the Easter Island natives. They also stood as symbols of status, showing that the commissioner had the power and wealth to hire the workers necessary to have one made and transported. While the Statues could be moved at a quick pace with less than twenty people, it took nearly three hundred more workers to feed and create tools for those transporting the enormous stone structures.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Moai Statues{/color} add a bonus production to every water tile in the city in which it's constructed. It also increases the chances of a {color:unit_text}Great Prophet{/color} appearing.

name: Moat
pedia: A moat is a deep, broad ditch, either dry or filled with water, that surrounds a castle, building or town, historically to provide it with a preliminary line of defense. Unfortuantly, a moat's stagnant water breeds bacteria that increases a cities unhealthiness.
strategy: A Moat will force enemies to confront your city head on, or retreat!

name: Grain Silo
pedia: Early humans were nomadic, settling in specific regions only for brief periods of time. When the food supply was exhausted in one area, the nomads would move on to search for more. Cities became possible only when the development of agriculture made the supply of food more abundant and dependable. However, cities still needed a way to keep the food supply stable throughout all four seasons. To do so, the citizens had to come up with a way to store seasonal crops for later use. The Granary was designed for the storage and protection of surplus food. Food storage technology meant that a smaller percentage of the population could produce and store enough food for everyone, allowing the remainder to pursue other jobs and activities.
strategy: {color:building_text}Modern Granaries{/color} store food to help increase a city's growth rate. They add additional health if your civ has access to {color:highlight_text}Corn{/color}, {color:highlight_text}Wheat{/color}, {color:highlight_text}Rice{/color}, and {color:highlight_text}Potato{/color}.

name: Ger
pedia: As nomadic tribesmen (and later as cavalry-based conquerors), the Mongolians' survival was dependent upon the quality of their horses and the skill of their riders.  A warhorse must be extensively trained if it is to be successfully used in battle. In their natural state, most horses quite sensibly seek to run away from dangerous situations - say, when surrounded by screaming men armed with sharp objects. A cavalryman's horse, on the other hand, needs to be able to suppress this instinct and instead instantly carry out any order given it by its rider - no matter how suicidal. Such training takes time and skill - for both mount and rider. Mongolian stables - built in the ubiquitous Mongolian yurt (or "ger") tents - provide such training.
strategy: {color:building_text}Gers{/color}, the Mongol replacements for {color:building_text}Stables{/color}, provide your mounted units with even more experience than {color:building_text}Stables{/color}.

name: Cinema
pedia: Most movie theaters are commercial operations catering to the general public, who attend by purchasing a ticket. The movie is projected with a movie projector onto a large projection screen at the front of the auditorium. Some movie theaters are now equipped for digital cinema projection, removing the need to create and transport a physical film print.
strategy: Movies can make people happy and some might even become celebrities.

name: Mt. Rushmore
pedia: Mount Rushmore stands as one of the largest sculpted structures in modern human history. Mount Rushmore displays in granite the heads of four great US presidents: George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Abraham Lincoln, and Theodore Roosevelt. Each head stands approximately 60 feet in height. [PARAGRAPH:2]Mount Rushmore was the vision of Doane Robinson, the superintendent of the South Dakota Historical Society. He engaged the famous American sculptor Gutzon Borglum to take charge of the project. For fourteen years Borglum and a team of 400 local miners blasted, chiseled, scraped and polished the granite mountain until the work was finally completed in 1941. Most remarkably, no one was killed during construction. [PARAGRAPH:2]Mount Rushmore has been called the "American Shrine." Each year thousands journey to the rugged mountains of South Dakota to look upon their four great leaders.
strategy: {color:building_text}Mount Rushmore{/color} decreases war weariness in all cities in your civilization and increases its city's chances of generating a {color:unit_text}Great Artist{/color}.

name: Museum
pedia: A museum is a "permanent institution in the service of society and of its development, open to the public, which acquires, conserves, researches, communicates and exhibits the tangible and intangible heritage of humanity and its environment, for the purposes of education, study, and enjoyment", as defined by the International Council of Museums.
strategy: A place for your people to go to learn about their history and cultural heritage. Ticket sales give small income bonus.

name: Myth of the Beast
pedia: A "myth" is a story used to explain a natural phenomena, historical legend, or customary practice. Myths can be elaborations on historical events or allegories to explain parts of the world like the movement of the sun and moon or the behavior of animals. A "mythology" is a body of myths that forms a key part of a civilization's culture. Every ancient civilizations had their own mythology, and scholars have developed models of comparison between them to discover how myths began.
strategy: {color:building_text}Myth of the Beast{/color} provides a small amount of Food, Production, and Commerce. It requires a {color:unit_text}Captured Animal{/color} to build.

name: Myth of the Hero
pedia: A "myth" is a story used to explain a natural phenomena, historical legend, or customary practice. Myths can be elaborations on historical events or allegories to explain parts of the world like the movement of the sun and moon or the behavior of animals. A "mythology" is a body of myths that forms a key part of a civilization's culture. Every ancient civilizations had their own mythology, and scholars have developed models of comparison between them to discover how myths began.
strategy: {color:building_text}Myth of the Hero{/color} provides a small amount of Production and Science. It can be built once you have a Level 3 Unit and is incompatible with other Myths.

name: Myth of the Sea
pedia: A "myth" is a story used to explain a natural phenomena, historical legend, or customary practice. Myths can be elaborations on historical events or allegories to explain parts of the world like the movement of the sun and moon or the behavior of animals. A "mythology" is a body of myths that forms a key part of a civilization's culture. Every ancient civilizations had their own mythology, and scholars have developed models of comparison between them to discover how myths began.
strategy: {color:building_text}Myth of the Sea{/color} provides a small amount of Food and Science. It can be built in a coastal city and is incompatible with other Myths.

name: Myth of the Sky
pedia: A "myth" is a story used to explain a natural phenomena, historical legend, or customary practice. Myths can be elaborations on historical events or allegories to explain parts of the world like the movement of the sun and moon or the behavior of animals. A "mythology" is a body of myths that forms a key part of a civilization's culture. Every ancient civilizations had their own mythology, and scholars have developed models of comparison between them to discover how myths began.
strategy: {color:building_text}Myth of the Sky{/color} provides a small amount of Commerce and Science. It can be built in a city with a nearby Peak and is incompatible with other Myths.

help: {icon:bullet}Defuses all nuclear weapons from all civilizations (one time effect)
name: Nanite Defuser
strategy: Nanite Defuser disarms all nukes from all players, increases defense in all cities and decreases enemies' war weariness.

name: Nanite Lab
strategy: Nanite Lab produces Nanobots which are required for Nanofactory and Nanite Clouds.

name: Utility Fog
pedia: Utility Fog is a collection of tiny robots together performing a certain function. The idea of nanobotic swarms was detailed as early as in 1964 by Stanislaw Lem in the novel The Invincible, and explored in some recent SciFi novels, such as Prey (2002), written by Michael Crichton. When self-replication is taken as an additional feature of such devices, the possibility of losing control of the swarm is the basis of post-apocalyptic scenarios such as the Grey goo.
strategy: Utility Fog increases city's production, defense and health.

name: Nano Research Department
strategy: Nano Research Department increases city's science and produces Nanotubes.

name: Nanofactory
pedia: A nanofactory is a system in which nanomachines (resembling molecular assemblers, or industrial robot arms) would combine reactive molecules via mechanosynthesis to build larger atomically precise parts. These, in turn, would be assembled by positioning mechanisms of assorted sizes to build macroscopic (visible) but still atomically-precise products.
strategy: Nanofactory increases city's production.

name: National Epic
pedia: An "epic" is a heroic poem celebrating the life and achievements of a heroic individual or group. Classic examples of epics include Homer's "Iliad" and "Odyssey." [PARAGRAPH:1]A "national epic" celebrates the exploits of an entire country. One of the earliest examples is the "Shahnama," (The Book of Kings), a Persian literary classic written around 1000 AD. The Shahnama chronicles the history of Persia from mythological pre-history through the reign of Khosrau II (590-628). The work contains over 60,000 couplets and is still read and enjoyed by modern readers. [PARAGRAPH:1]It is possible that the age of the literary epic is dead, and that in the future all such stories will be done as "made for TV movies." This would be a great misfortune to the world of letters - and to the rest of the world, as well.
strategy: The {color:building_text}National Epic{/color} greatly increases the rate at which its city produces {color:highlight_text}Great People{/color}, particularly {color:unit_text}Great Artists{/color}.

name: National Mint
pedia:
A mint is an industrial facility which manufactures coins for currency.
The history of mints correlates closely with the history of coins. One difference is that the history of the mint is normally related in a fashion that more closely ties to the political situation of an era. For example, when discussing the history of the New Orleans Mint, the usage of that mint by the Confederate States of America beginning in 1861 is a notable occurrence. The origins of the Philadelphia Mint, which began operations in 1792 and first produced circulating coinage in 1793, are often related within the political context of the time.
In the beginning, hammered coinage or cast coinage were the chief means of coin minting, with resulting production runs numbering as little as the hundreds or thousands. In modern mints, coin dies are manufactured in large numbers and planchets are made into milled coins by the billions.
With the mass production of currency the production cost is weighed when minting coins. For example, it costs the US Mint much less than 25 cents to make a quarter, and the difference in production cost and face value (called seigniorage) helps fund the minting body.
strategy: Build A Mint when you have access to lots of rare metals

name: National Park
pedia: While areas of great natural beauty had often been protected or revered in the past, the modern conception of a National Park did not appear until 1872. Yellowstone National Park, located in the western United States, departed from previous nature preserves - which tended to be set aside for nobility - by opening up the land for the enjoyment of the public. After the creation of Yellowstone, National Parks began popping up throughout the world.
strategy: Build the {color:building_text}National Park{/color} to eliminate all unhealthiness from population in your city. It also provides a free specialist for each {color:highlight_text}Forest Preserve{/color} in its city radius and increases the chances that a {color:unit_text}Great Scientist{/color} might appear in your city.

name: National Redoubt
pedia: Nations have always built fortresses and fixed defenses for potential last stands during wartime. These defenses offer a single, heavily guarded and fortified location for military and political leaders to retreat to in the hopes of creating a strongpoint too difficult to defeat.[PARAGRAPH:2]One of the most famous examples of the concept of a national redoubt was in Germany during the waning days of World War II. German radio broadcasts would speak of a redoubt hidden in the Bavarian Alps, and much Allied planning was spent to neutralize this non-existent redoubt instead of attempting to race the Soviets to Berlin.
strategy: The {color:building_text}National Redoubt{/color} greatly increases the building city's defense, including against air and espionage. It also grants the {color:highlight_text}Stealth I{/color} promotion to units built there.

name: Security Bureau
pedia: As long as there has been espionage, there has been a need for counter-espionage. This is the realm of the Security Bureau. Bureaus like the American FBI or the British MI5 make sure that sensitive intelligence is protected from outside sources. While espionage is an ancient practice, most Security Bureaus are less than one hundred years old. MI5 has only been in existence since 1909, organized originally to fight against German spies before World War I. The FBI began its expansion in the 1930s thanks to J. Edgar Hoover, the Bureau's first director.
strategy: Build a {color:building_text}Security Bureau{/color} to increase the cost of enemy espionage missions in your city.

name: National Shield
strategy: National Shield gives Advanced Shielding to all your cities and upgrades all Anti-Missile Batteries, Arcologies and Arcology Shielding buildings to Advanced Shielding.

name: Broadcast Network
pedia: A television station is a type of broadcast station that broadcasts both audio and video to television receivers in a particular area. Traditionally, TV stations made their broadcasts by sending specially-encoded radio signals over the air, called terrestrial television. Individual television stations are usually granted licenses by a government agency to use a particular section of the radio spectrum (a channel) through which they send their signals. Some stations use LPTV broadcast translators to retransmit to further areas. Many television stations are now in the process of converting from analogue (NTSC, PAL, or SECAM) to digital TV (ATSC, DVB, or ISDB).

name: Totem Pole
pedia: Totem Poles were a tradition of the Native American tribes of the Pacific Northwest. Built from Oregon to Alaska, the Totem Pole is a visual representation of various tribal legends or important occurrences. [PARAGRAPH:1]While not worshipped, Totem Poles were often revered as symbols of wealth and common heritage. Yet some Totem Poles acted as warnings, rather than testaments. "Shame Poles" could be constructed to remind a tribe of a particular debt or offense. One particularly controversial pole, now found in the Alaska State Museum, bears the image of President Abraham Lincoln. Some claim that the "Lincoln Pole" was built to honor the passage of the Emancipation Proclamation, while many believe that it was built to mourn the wealth lost by the Tlingits tribe when forced to free their slaves.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Totem Pole{/color}, the Native American replacement for the {color:building_text}Monument{/color}, grants archery units three bonus experience in addition to the usual culture bonus.

name: Naval Academy
strategy: Naval Academy provides experience and gives {color:highlight_text}Navigation I{/color} promotion to new ships.

name: Naval Yard
strategy: Increases city's naval production and gives 4 free experience for new ships.

name: Dike
pedia: Dikes are walls of earth or stone, used to entrap or hold back water. Often built as a protection against flooding, the dike has come to characterize the Netherlands, with significant portions of the country actually lying below sea level. Dikes, while a necessity for the country's continued survival (and independence from foreign towel imports), were occasionally used as a clever tactic for self-defense. During the Siege of Leiden in the midst of the Eighty Years War, Dutch leader Willem van Oranje's men cut the dykes around the city, flooding the positions of the opposing Spanish and driving the invaders back before the sea.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Dike{/color}, the Dutch replacement for the {color:building_text}Levee{/color}, provides a production bonus from all water tiles worked by a city, in addition to river tiles.

name: Network Node
Neuschwanstein
pedia: Neuschwanstein is a 19th-century Bavarian palace on a rugged hill near Hohenschwangau and Füssen in southwest Bavaria, Germany. The palace was commissioned by Ludwig II of Bavaria as a retreat and as an homage to Richard Wagner, the King's inspiring muse.  Ludwig did not allow visitors to his castles, but after his death in 1886 the castle was opened to the public.
strategy: {color:building_text}Neuschwanstein{/color} Initiates a Golden Age and gives all cities on the continent +1 Happiness.

name: Isaac Newton's College
pedia: Sir Isaac Newton, a mathematician and physicist, is considered to be one of the greatest scientists of all time. He is credited with many important discoveries including the laws of gravity, the color spectrum of light, calculus, fluid dynamics, and an understanding of ocean tides. He also built the world's first reflecting telescope. For 32 years, he held the position of Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge University, an important teaching post, where he continued his own research while instructing a generation of students.
strategy: {color:building_text}Newton's University{/color} provides a large science boost in the city where it is built. Can not be built in same city as Copernicus Observatory or Leonardo's Workshop.

name: National Sports League
strategy: National Sports League increases culture in all cities by 10% and grants +2 free celebrities in the city it's built.

name: Stockfish
pedia: Beside oil, gas, and income from the merchant fleet, stockfish is Norway's longest sustained export commodity, and the socioeconomically most profitable export over the centuries.  Stockfish is unsalted fish, especially cod, dried by sun and wind on wooden racks on the foreshore called flakes, or in special drying houses. The drying of food  is the world's oldest known preservation method, and dried fish has a storage life of several years. The method is cheap and effective in suitable climates, the work can be done by the fisherman and family, and the resulting product is easily transported to market.  Cod is the most common fish used in stockfish production, while other whitefish, such as pollock, haddock, ling and tusk, are used to a lesser degree.  Over the centuries, several variants of stockfish have evolved, notably salt cod. Salting was not economically feasible before the 17th century, when cheap salt from southern Europe became available to the maritime nations of northern Europe.
strategy: {color:building_text}Stockfish{/color} is great for growth, if you have the resources.

name: Notre Dame
pedia: Notre Dame is a mighty cathedral standing on the "Ile de la Citie," an island in the Seine River in Paris, France. Built on the site of an older church, which was in turn built on the site of a Roman temple to Jupiter, Notre Dame is a magnificent example of gothic architecture and one of the greatest buildings standing. Construction of Notre Dame began in 1163 and took almost two centuries to complete. [PARAGRAPH:2]Notre Dame is a massive stone building of square towers, flying buttresses, and tall spires. The exterior of the building is decorated with delicate ribbons of arches and statues of saints and kings. The roofline of the building is festooned with gargoyles. The interior of the cathedral is a long, narrow space with columns lining each side, supporting two beautiful raised galleries. Brilliant stained glass windows shine gently down on the main altar, which contains a beautiful statue of the Virgin Mary, the cathedral's patron, holding the body of Jesus. [PARAGRAPH:2]The cathedral has suffered many periods of neglect over the years. During the French Revolution, many of Notre Dame's treasures were stolen and the building was used as a warehouse. In the early 1800s, the cathedral was in such a state of disrepair that the city planners contemplated tearing it down. In fact, Victor Hugo wrote "The Hunchback of Notre Dame" in part to raise awareness of the cathedral's plight. In 1871, during the short-lived Paris Commune, Notre Dame was almost set on fire. [PARAGRAPH:2]Fortunately the cathedral survived it all, and has now been largely restored to its original grandeur.
strategy: {color:building_text}Notre Dame{/color} increases the happiness of all of your cities built on the same continent. It increases its city's chances of generating a {color:unit_text}Great Artist{/color}.

name: Nuclear Plant
pedia: Nuclear power plants utilize radioactive materials and the process of nuclear fission to generate the heat and steam needed to run electrical generators and produce electricity. Because nuclear power doesn't cause the air pollution associated with the burning of coal or petroleum products, this means of generating power is considered a viable alternative energy source. However, the toxic nature of the byproducts produced by the fission process creates serious problems of its own. No method of safely disposing of this toxic waste has been found, and the volatile nature of the fission reaction can lead to a meltdown of the reactor core if the reaction is not properly controlled. Because of these problems, the future of nuclear power is uncertain.
strategy: With access to {color:highlight_text}Uranium{/color}, {color:building_text}Nuclear Plants{/color} provide power for {color:building_text}Factories{/color}.

help: {icon:bullet}Prevents Random Weather Events
name: National Weather Service
pedia: The National Weather Service (NWS), is one of the six scientific agencies that make up the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) of the United States government. It is tasked with providing "weather, hydrologic, and climate forecasts and warnings for the United States, its territories, adjacent waters and ocean areas, for the protection of life and property and the enhancement of the national economy." This is done through a collection of national and regional centers, and 122 local weather forecast offices (WFOs).
strategy: The National Weather Service organizes all weather forecasts and models for all other cities. It will grant all existing and new units the ability to use weather forecasting to aid their combat abilites, a sizeable advantage in any war.

name: Monument
pedia: A monument is a structure that reminds people of an important event that occured in the area, or an important person - a famous general or leader, perhaps. Different cultures have constructed monuments out of varied materials - wood, stone, or even precious metals. Generally, the only ancient monuments remaining today are those made out of stone: over time the wooden monuments have decayed, and the ones constructed of precious metals have been looted and destroyed.
strategy: {color:building_text}Monuments{/color} provide a small amount of culture, and are a good way to expand city borders early on.

name: Observatory
pedia: An observatory is a building designed to allow those inside to study the stars, usually with the aid of a telescope. Early observatories consisted of buildings with conveniently-placed windows or high platforms, while later models have sophisticated rotating roofs with an aperture to hold a massive telescope. The rooftop rotates to allow the telescope to point in any direction. [PARAGRAPH:1]An observatory's location has much to do with its efficacy. Smog and other pollutants cut down on visibility; further, stars become more difficult to observe when there are other light-sources visible; so modern observatories are usually built as far away from cities as practical.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Observatory{/color} increases a city's scientific research. It is required to build a {color:building_text}Laboratory{/color}.

name: Oil Power Plant
strategy: Oil Power Plant provides power with Oil resource

name: Oil Refinery
pedia: An oil refinery is an industrial process plant where crude oil is processed and refined into more useful petroleum products, such as gasoline, diesel fuel, asphalt base, heating oil, kerosine, and liquefied petroleum gas. Oil refineries are typically large sprawling industrial complexes with extensive piping running throughout, carrying streams of fluids between large chemical processing units.
strategy: Oil Refinery turns crude oil to {color:highlight_text}Oil Products{/color}.

name: Olympic Games
pedia: The Olympic Games (often referred to simply as The Olympics or The Games) is an international multi-sport event subdivided into summer and winter sporting events. The summer and winter games are each held every four years (an Olympiad). Until 1992, they were both held in the same year. Since then, they have been separated two years apart. [PARAGRAPH:1]The original Olympic Games began in 776 BC in Olympia, Greece, and was celebrated until AD 393. Interest in reviving the Olympic Games proper was first shown by the Greek poet and newspaper editor Panagiotis Soutsos in his poem "Dialogue of the Dead" in 1833. Evangelos Zappas sponsored the first modern international Olympic Games in 1859. He paid for the refurbishment of the Panathinaiko Stadium for Games held there in 1870 and 1875. This was noted in newspapers and publications around the world including the London Review, which stated that "the Olympian Games, discontinued for centuries, have recently been revived! Here is strange news indeed ... the classical games of antiquity were revived near Athens".
strategy: Olympic Games grants free Arena in all cities and increases culture and happiness in the city where it's built.

name: Omnifactory
pedia: The Omnifactory is a robotic factory that can produce virtually anything. Using nanobots and replicators, the Omnifactory assembles components and finished goods from the atomic level up.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Omnifactory{/color} is the civic building for the {color:highlight_text}Post-Scarcity{/color} civic. It replaces almost all previous production buildings and provides copies of many manufactured resources.

name: Opera House
pedia: An opera house is a theater building used for opera performances that consists of a stage, an orchestra pit, audience seating, and backstage facilities for costumes and set building. While some venues are constructed specifically for operas, other opera houses are part of larger performing arts centers.[PARAGRAPH:2]The first public opera house was the Teatro San Cassiano in Venice, Italy, which opened in 1637. Italy, where opera has been popular through the centuries among ordinary people as well as wealthy patrons, still has a large number of opera houses.  When Henry Purcell was composing, there was no opera house in London. The first opera house in Germany was built in Hamburg 1678. Early U.S. opera houses served a variety of functions in towns and cities, hosting community dances, fairs, plays, and vaudeville shows as well as operas and other musical events.  In the 17th and 18th centuries, opera houses were often financed by rulers, nobles, and wealthy people who used patronage of the arts to endorse their political ambitions and social positions or prestige. With the rise of bourgeois and capitalist social forms in the 19th century, European culture moved away from its patronage system to a publicly-supported system. In the 2000s, most opera and theaters raise funds from a combination of government and institutional grants, ticket sales and, to a smaller extent, private donations.
strategy: Opera Houses increase happiness and culture in the cities.

name: The Oracle
pedia: In ancient Greek religion, an oracle was a priest or priestess through whom the gods spoke in response to questions. The oracle interpreted dreams, the actions of entranced persons, and physical signs found in the entrails of sacrificed animals. The most famous oracle resided in the shrine of Apollo at Delphi, located on the slopes of Mount Parnassus. Greeks, Romans, and others consulted this oracle for centuries about public policy and private matters. A priestess called the Pythia would, for a fee, make public predictions for the future. These ecstatic pronouncements became infamous for their ambiguity.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Oracle{/color} gives the builder one free technology advance, and it increases the odds of its city generating a {color:unit_text}Great Prophet{/color}.

name: Orbital Factory
strategy: Orbital Factory increases city's base food and production output.

name: Orbital Hotel
pedia: An orbital hotel is a place for space tourists to sleep for the night if they do not wish to undergo re-entry until tomorrow or just need a rest.
strategy: Orbital Hotel increases happiness and commerce in all your cities and provides extra commerce and culture in city where it's built.

name: Orbital Observatory
pedia: Attempts to observe outer space from the ground run into numerous problems. Light pollution from nearby cities interferes with observation. Atmospheric layers distort light from distant objects. Earth's atmosphere also absorbs X-rays, gamma rays, and ultraviolet frequencies, preventing them from being studied. Observatories in space avoid all of these difficulties. The most famous example is the Hubble Space Telescope.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Orbital Observatory{/color} provides additional science to the city where it is built.

name: Hammam
pedia:
Cleanliness was extremely important in Ottoman culture. Before modern plumbing, the Ottomans constructed communal steam baths ("hammams") throughout their major cities. In early times many of these were attached to mosques - ritual cleanliness played an important part in the Ottoman religious beliefs - in later periods they evolved into separate buildings and eventually, into enormous complexes of buildings.

The Ottoman hammams were largely modeled on their Roman and Byzantine predecessors. They contained three main areas: a hot room, a moderate room and a cool room. Both men and women could attend hammams, but they bathed in separate areas.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Hammam{/color}, the Ottoman replacement for the {color:building_text}Aqueduct{/color}, improves a city's happiness and health. Build {color:building_text}Hammams{/color} when you want to grow a city, or when the populace begins clamoring for it.

name: Oxford University
pedia: The University of Oxford, England, is the oldest university in the English-speaking world. It is also one of the most prestigious. The exact date of the university's founding is unknown, but scholars believe it was some time around 1100 AD. [PARAGRAPH:1]Oxford is made up of 39 colleges and seven "permanent private halls" (which are religious organizations). Each is housed in a separate building usually built in a square around a quadrangle. The colleges generally consist of a great hall, a chapel, a library, a bar, several common rooms, classrooms, and lodging for around 300 students. Built in the 1250s, Balliol, Merton, and University Colleges are among the oldest. [PARAGRAPH:1]For most of its existence, Oxford has been one of the world's great universities, and it remains so to this day. Many famous people have passed through its halls, including four English and eight foreign kings, over 50 presidents and prime ministers (including US President William Clinton), 47 Nobel Prize winners, and one pope.
strategy: {color:building_text}Oxford University{/color} greatly increases the scientific output of its city. It also allows you to change three citizens into scientists and increases its city's chance of generating a {color:unit_text}Great Scientist{/color}.

name: Painter's Studio
pedia: Painting has been around for centuries as a way to record the appearances of persons, scenes, or other subjects. During the Renaissance, great strides were made in realism and detail, capturing various subjects as true to life as possible. The rise of photography led to the diversification of portrait painting, as the camera could compete with simple portraits.
strategy: {color:building_text}Painter's Studio{/color} provides a small amount of gold and culture, along with an Artist specialist slot.

name: Palace
pedia: When populations began to organize their communities into cities, their governments became more structured and formalized. At an early stage, the ruler of the city established headquarters from which the business of running the city was conducted. In many cases, these buildings also served as the living quarters of the ruler. In wealthy cities, these facilities often expanded into immense, sprawling palaces. These richly adorned, imposing buildings were a source of civic pride, and helped to reinforce the aura of power surrounding the ruler.
strategy: The city containing the {color:building_text}Palace{/color} is the capital of your civilization and city maintenance is decreased in cities near it. The {color:building_text}Palace{/color} generates culture and a small amount of commerce.

name: Palisade
pedia: A palisade is a wall made from wooden stakes or tree trunks. The wooden posts are driven into the ground and sharpened at the top to prevent climbing over them. Palisades made for excellent quick defenses until more substantial fortifications could be built, and it was even possible to make portable palisades to protect armies on the march.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Palisade{/color} provides cheap early defense until it is replaced by {color:building_text}Walls{/color}.

name: Paper Mill
pedia: Paper mills are factories that create paper from plant fibers, either cloth or wood. The most successful paper mills developed in the late 13th century and used water to drive the mill machinery. Paper mills consisted of two major parts; the pulp mill that converted the plant products to pulp and the paper mill itself that turned the pulp into usable paper. The pulping process was responsible for most of the odors and noise associated with paper mills.
strategy: Build {color:building_text}Paper Mill{/color} to produce {color:highlight_text}Paper{/color}, which increases the production of {color:building_text}Libraries{/color}, {color:building_text}Universities{/color}, and other science buildings.

name: Paradise Garden
strategy: Paradise Garden gives +2 free specialists to the city and increases happiness.

name: Park Arcology
pedia: With growing populations, Ecotopias decided that they too had to build arcologies, but took great care to not harm the environment.  Their arcologies were designed to be entirely self-sufficient and produce no pollution, which required people to grow their own food, make their own clothes, and create their own energy from natural sources.
strategy: Provides a little Culture, reduces Gold, and nullifies building pollution.  This building requires Paradise civic.

name: Parthenon
pedia: The Parthenon was constructed in 433 BC, in Athens, Greece, in honor of Athens' patron goddess, Athena. Measuring 100 feet by 225 feet, the Parthenon is constructed almost totally of marble. The exterior of the Parthenon is ringed with Doric-style columns more than 30 feet in height, and the center part of the temple, called the "cella," is a large open space which once held a statue of Athena. Much of the temple was decorated with beautiful marble statues and friezes celebrating Athena and the glories of Athens. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Parthenon has suffered much from the ravages of time. In the 5th century a Roman Emperor stole the statue of Athena and moved it to Constantinople, where it was subsequently destroyed. In the 13th century the Parthenon was converted to a Catholic church, which involved altering the internal structure and removing (and probably destroying) many statues dedicated to the old gods. In the 15th century Athens was captured by the Ottomans, and the temple was turned into a mosque. In the 17th century the Parthenon was partially destroyed during a war between the Ottomans and Venetians. Finally, in the 19th century, the British ambassador to Greece looted all of the surviving marble friezes from the building, which he subsequently sold to the British museum. [PARAGRAPH:2]Despite the centuries of neglect, mutilation and pillaging, the Parthenon still stands - a remarkably powerful and beautiful symbol of the glories of ancient Greece.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Parthenon{/color} increases the rate at which your civilization generates {color:highlight_text}Great People{/color}, particularly {color:unit_text}Great Artists{/color}. It also has a high cultural value.

name: Peace Movement
pedia: Peace movements are organizations that seek to end wars and violence in society. The first non-religious movements arose following the Enlightenment and the Napoleonic Wars. Peace movements were founded in New Work in 1815 and London in 1816, with an International Peace Conference held in London in 1843. Peace movements had a great surge in popularity following the immense casualties of the First World War and even more movements sprang up following the use of nuclear weapons in World War II and the long-running, poorly-defined Vietnam War.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Peace Movement{/color} is the civic building for the {color:highlight_text}Pacifism{/color} civic. Each Peace Movement increases War Weariness for you and for any civilization you are at war with by 5%, cumulatively, so enough of them can make it very difficult for any civilization to go to war with you.

name: Pentagon
pedia: The Pentagon is the largest office building in existence. The structure was completed on January 15, 1943, during the height of the Second World War, after a crash building effort of only 16 months. The 83 million dollar facility covers more than six million square feet, roughly three times that of the Chicago's Sears Tower (the second largest office building). Originally a US Army facility, it soon became the nerve center for all military branches of the United States.
strategy: Once the {color:building_text}Pentagon{/color} is built, all new units built in your civilization receive two experience points and increases the chance that its city more likely to generate a {color:unit_text}Great Spy{/color}.

name: Satrap
pedia: A satrap was a provincial governor of the first Persian Empire. While other empires had client kings, the Persians did not allow the use of the title king for anyone except the Persian emperor himself. The satraps were viceroys, ruling in the name of the king and wielding some power, including military force. Certain members of each satrap's court were royal officials reporting to the king instead of the satrap, serving as a check on the satrap's power. Several successors to the Persian Empire would use the title of satrap as well. The term satrap survives to this day to refer to a leader who is really no more than another nation's puppet.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Satrap{/color} is the Persian replacement for a {color:building_text}Courthouse{/color}. It not only decreases city maintenance, but also increases Happiness, allowing you to build a larger and more productive empire.

name: Personal Rapid Train
strategy: Personal Rapid Train increases health and happiness in the city.

name: Petra
pedia: Petra is an archaeological site in southwestern Jordan, lying on the slope of Mount Hor in a basin among the mountains which form the eastern flank of Arabah (Wadi Araba), the large valley running from the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Aqaba. It is renowned for its rock-cut architecture. [PARAGRAPH:1]The site remained unknown to the Western world until 1812, when it was discovered by Swiss explorer Johann Ludwig Burckhardt. It was famously described as "a rose-red city half as old as time" in a Newdigate prize-winning sonnet by John William Burgon. UNESCO has described it as "one of the most precious cultural properties of man's cultural heritage." In 1985, Petra was designated a World Heritage Site. It is one of the "New Seven Wonders of the World" as determined by the New Open World Corporation (not affiliated with UNESCO).
strategy: Petra grants +1 free trade route in all cities and 1 free priest in the city where it's built.

name: Pharmacy
pedia: A pharmacy (commonly the chemist in Australia, New Zealand and the UK; or drugstore in North America; retail pharmacy in industry terminology; or Apothecary, historically) is the place where most pharmacists practice the profession of pharmacy. It is the community pharmacy where the dichotomy of the profession exists-health professionals who are also retailers. [PARAGRAPH:2]Community pharmacies usually consist of a retail storefront with a dispensary where medications are stored and dispensed. The dispensary is subject to pharmacy legislation; with requirements for storage conditions, compulsory texts, equipment, etc., specified in legislation. Where it was once the case that pharmacists stayed within the dispensary compounding/dispensing medications; there has been an increasing trend towards the use of trained pharmacy technicians while the pharmacist spends more time communicating with patients.[PARAGRAPH:2]All pharmacies are required to have a pharmacist on-duty at all times when open. In many jurisdictions, it is also a requirement that the owner of a pharmacy must be a registered pharmacist (R.Ph.). This latter requirement has been revoked in many jurisdictions, such that many retailers (including supermarkets and mass merchandisers) now include a pharmacy as a department of their store.[PARAGRAPH:2]Likewise, many pharmacies are now rather grocery store-like in their design. In addition to medicines and prescriptions, many now sell a diverse arrangement of additional household items such as cosmetics, shampoo, office supplies, confectionary, and snack foods.

name: Photographer's Studio
pedia: Portrait photography was a popular use for cameras almost as soon as they were developed. The rising middle class during the Industrial Revolution wanted portraits, and painters could not meet the demand. Early cameras were bulky and needed long exposure times, as well as needing specialized chemical processes for developing the photographs. The artist's studio evolved into the photographic studio to meet these needs.
strategy: {color:building_text}Photographer's Studio{/color} provides an Artist specialist slot and a small amount of Gold and Culture.

name: Crannog
pedia: A crannog is the name given in Scotland and Ireland to an artificial island or natural island, used for a settlement. The name can also be used to refer to wooden platforms erected on shallow loch floors, although understandably few remains of this sort have been found.[PARAGRAPH:1]The choice of an island as a home is thought to have been for defence as well as the availability of food in the form of fish nearby. The crannog could be reached from the nearest shore by means of a causeway built up with stones, or else a wooden gangway built atop raised piles.[PARAGRAPH:1]The islet of Eilean Domhnuill, Loch Olabhat on North Uist may be the earliest crannóg, dated to 3200-2800 BC in the Neolithic period. Most crannógs were in use from the Iron Age through to the early Medieval period, at about the same time as the brochs, the wags, duns and the larger roundhouses.[PARAGRAPH:1]
strategy: A {color:building_text}Crannog{/color} (the Pictish replacement for a {color:building_text}Harbor{/color}) increases that city's income from trade routes and extra defense. It increases a city's health from access to {color:highlight_text}Clam{/color}, {color:highlight_text}Crab{/color}, and {color:highlight_text}Fish{/color} resources.

name: Leaning Tower
pedia: Although intended to stand vertically, the tower began leaning to the southeast soon after the onset of construction in 1173 due sandy soil.  In 1272, construction resumed under Giovanni di Simone, architect of the Camposanto. In an effort to compensate for the tilt, the engineers built higher floors with one side taller than the other. This made the tower begin to lean in the other direction. Because of this, the tower is actually curved.
strategy: {color:building_text}Leaning Tower of Pisa{/color} Increases Great Person and Culture rates in all cities.

name: Plague Hospital
pedia: A plague hospital is an old institution where victims of various contagions are quarantined.  The Abbassids realized that disease spread from person to person, and wrote the first accurate descriptions of measles and smallpox. To respond to this, they built clean hospitals to treat victims of disease.  Lazzaretti in Italy where used to quarantine sailors to stop the spread of the Bubonic Plague; eventually, any plague victims where placed there.  Lazzaretti were also used as a model for quarantining syphilitics after it spread to Italy in 1494.
strategy: Increases Health, greatly increases Health with resources.  This building requires Charity civic.

name: Planning Office
pedia: Legions of bureaucrats and party members are required to run a planned economy.  Quotas need to be created and monitored, and these offices are in charge of this important task.
strategy: Reduces Maintenance, but also Commerce.  Slight Production increase.  This building requires Planned civic.

name: Plato's Academy
pedia: The word "academy" is used today to refer to any institution of higher learning, but the name originally referred to the "Akademeia," a school in Athens, created approximately in 385 BC by the philosopher, Plato - having just returned to Athens after traveling across the Mediterranean, Plato founded the school so that he could disseminate his philosophy to a larger group of scholars. Plato's school was located in a grove of sacred olive trees; it was named after a legendary hero called, "Akademos."[PARAGRAPH:1]Plato's Academy was one of the earliest known schools in Western civilization. Among the many intellectuals who studied at the Academy, perhaps the most famous is Aristotle, who would become a legendary philosopher himself - and one of the primary developers of what is called "western thought." Plato's Academy continued to operate for many centuries until it was closed by the Emperor Justinian in 529 AD, who saw it as a pagan institution and a threat to the propagation of Christianity.
strategy: {color:building_text}Plato's Academy{/color} greatly increase a city's scientific research as well as its cultural output.

name: Pleistocene Park
pedia: Pleistocene Park is an attempt to recreate the ecosystems of the last Ice Age in northern Siberia. Efforts are currently focused on currently-living herbivores, with some work being done with carnivores. It is possible that cloning technology may advance to the point where extinct megafauna can be recreated. While this is not possible to do with dinosaurs, as DNA is not stable over the geologic time scales required, some of these mammals may have survived until only a few millenia ago.
strategy: {color:building_text}Pleistocene Park{/color} increases the happiness of all your cities and generates trade income.

name: Police Station
pedia: A police station is a building which serves as the headquarters of a police force or unit which serves a specific district. These buildings typically contain offices, various accommodations for their personnel and their vehicles such as locker rooms, temporary holding cells, and interview and interrogation rooms.
strategy: Police Station increases city's espionage and helps thwart rival spies. Reduces War Weariness in the city.

name: Polis Council
pedia: A polis is a city, a city-state and also citizenship and body of citizens. When used to describe Classical Athens and its contemporaries, polis is often translated as "city-state."  The word originates from the ancient Greek city-states, which developed during the Archaic period, the ancestor of city, state and citizenship, and persisted well into Roman times, when the equivalent Latin word was civitas, also meaning 'citizenhood', while municipium applied to a non-sovereign local entity. The term city-state which originated in English does not fully translate the Greek term. The poleis were not like other primordial ancient city-states like Tyre or Sidon, which were ruled by a king or a small oligarchy, but rather a political entity ruled by its body of citizens.
strategy: Increases Happiness and decreases city Maintenance

name: Folwark
pedia: Folwarks are giant Polish farms that were operated in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from the 14th century into the 20th.  They were used to produce a surplus of food.  The first folwarks were created on church and monastery owned grounds, but were later adopted by nobility and rich peasants.  The creation of folwarks was boosted by a growing demand for grain and its high profit. Folwark-based grain export was an important part of the economy of the Polish-Lithuanian commonwealth.  [PARAGRAPH: 1] The fall of agriculture goods prices in the end of the 17th century marked the start of a crisis for the folwark related economy.  The noble's attempt to increase use of folwarks only hurt the economic crisis more.  Until the 18th century, folwarks remained the basis for Polish noble's economic and political power.  After the abolition of serfdom in Poland, folwarks used paid labor.  Folwarks were abolished by the People's Republic of Poland with the PKWN decree of 6 September 1944 about agricultural reform
strategy: The {color:building_text}Folwark{/color}, the Polish replacement for the {color:building_text}Granary{/color}, offers bonus food.

name: District Office
pedia: A District Office is where voters cast their ballots in elections.  Since elections generally take place over a one- or two-day span on a periodic basis, often annual or longer, polling places are often located in facilities used for other purposes, such as schools, sports halls, local government offices, or even private homes, and will each serve a similar number of people. The area may be known as a ward, precinct, polling district or constituency. The polling place is staffed with officials (who may be called election judges, returning officers or other titles) who monitor the voting procedures and assist voters with the election process. Scrutineers (or poll-watchers) are independent or partisan observers who attend the poll to ensure the impartiality of the process.  The facility will be open between specified hours depending upon the type of election, and political activity by or on behalf of those standing in the ballot is usually prohibited within the venue and immediately surrounding area.  Inside the polling place, will be an area (usually a voting booth) where the voter may select the candidate or party of their choice in secret, and if a ballot paper is used this will be placed into a ballot box in front of witnesses but who cannot see the actual selection made. Voting machines may be employed instead.  Some polling places are temporary structures. A portable cabin may be specially sited for an election and removed afterwards.
strategy: Reduces Maintenance and increases Happiness, but increases War Weariness.  This building requires Democracy civic.

name: Pont du Gard
pedia: The Pont du Gard is an aqueduct in the South of France constructed by the Roman Empire, and located in Vers-Pont-du-Gard near Remoulins, in the Gard département. Built on three levels, the Pont is 49 m high, and the longest level is 275 m (300 yards) long. On its first level, it carries a road and at the top of the third level, a water conduit, which is 1.8 metres (6 ft) high and 1.2 meters (4 ft) wide and has a gradient of 0.4 percent.[PARAGRAPH:2]It has long been thought that the Pont du Gard was built by Augustus' son-in-law and aide, Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, around the year 19 BC. Newer excavations, however, suggest the construction may have taken place in the middle of the first century A.D, consequently, opinion is now somewhat divided on the matter. Designed to carry the water across the small Gardon river valley, it was part of a nearly 50 km (31 mi) aqueduct that brought water from the Fontaines d'Eure springs near Uzès to the Castellum in the Roman city of Nemausus (Nîmes). The full aqueduct had a gradient of 34 cm/km (1/3000), descending only 17 m vertically in its entire length and delivering 20,000 cubic meters (5 million gallons) of water daily. [PARAGRAPH:2]It was constructed entirely without the use of mortar. The aqueduct's stones  some of which weigh up to 6 tons  were precisely cut to fit perfectly together eliminating the need for mortar. The masonry was lifted into place by block and tackle with a massive human-powered treadmill providing the power for the winch. A complex scaffold was erected to support the aqueduct as it was being built. The face of the aqueduct still bears the mark of its construction, in the form of protruding scaffolding supports and ridges on the piers which supported the semicircular wooden frames on which the arches were constructed. It is believed to have taken about three years to build, employing between 800 and 1,000 workers.
strategy: Pont du Gard grants +2 health in all cities on the same continent.

name: Porcelain Tower
pedia: The Porcelain Tower (or Porcelain Pagoda) of Nanjing also known as Bao'ensi (meaning "Temple of Gratitude"), is a historical site located on the south bank of the Yangtze in Nanjing, China. It was a pagoda constructed in the 15th century, but was mostly destroyed in the 19th century during the course of the Taiping rebellion. The tower is now under reconstruction.
strategy: {color:building_text} Porcelain Tower{/color} Increases Science and Gold in all cities.

name: Port
pedia: Just because a city is built in a coastal region doesn't guarantee that the city is readily accessible by ship. In order for a port city to establish a steady trade, fishing, or other shipping industry, the city must have a harbor. A harbor is a protected body of water that opens into an ocean or lake that shelters ships from waves and high winds. Although some coastal cities are established in areas where a natural harbor exists, most seaports are forced either to improve the existing natural harbor, or to build a man-made harbor to shelter ships and provide channels deep enough to accommodate large vessels.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Port{/color} increases that city's income from trade routes. It increases a city's health from access to {color:highlight_text}Clam{/color}, and {color:highlight_text}Crab{/color} resources.

name: Feitoria
pedia: The Feitoria is a Portuguese trading post. During the colonial era Feitorias were essential to the Portuguese in expanding their trade network between Europe, the Far East, and eventually the Americas. They afforded ships with limited range a safe port of call to refill depleted supplies and give their crews much needed rest.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Feitoria{/color}, the Portuguese replacement for the {color:building_text}Customs House{/color}, provides a commerce bonus from all water tiles worked by a city in addition to the usual foreign trade route bonus.

name: Palace of Potala
pedia: The Potala Palace is located in Lhasa, Tibet Autonomous Region. It was named after Mount Potala, the abode of Chenresig or Avalokitesvara. The Potala Palace was the chief residence of the Dalai Lama until the 14th Dalai Lama fled to Dharamsala, India, after an invasion and failed uprising in 1959. Today the Potala Palace has been converted into a museum by the Chinese. [PARAGRAPH:2]The building measures 400 metres east-west and 350 metres north-south, with sloping stone walls averaging 3 m. thick, and 5 m. (more than 16 ft) thick at the base, and with copper poured into the foundations to help proof it against earthquakes. Thirteen stories of buildings  containing over 1,000 rooms, 10,000 shrines and about 200,000 statues  soar 117 metres (384 ft) on top of Marpo Ri, the "Red Hill", rising more than 300 m (about 1,000 ft) in total above the valley floor. Tradition has it that the three main hills of Lhasa represent the "Three Protectors of Tibet." Chokpori, just to the south of the Potala, is the soul-mountain (bla-ri) of Vajrapani, Pongwari that of Manjushri, and Marpori, the hill on which the Potala stands, represents Chenresig or Avalokiteshvara.[PARAGRAPH:2]The site was used as a meditation retreat by King Songtsen Gampo, who in 637 built the first palace there in order to greet his bride Princess Wen Cheng of the Tang Dynasty of China. Lozang Gyatso, the Great Fifth Dalai Lama, started the construction of the Potala Palace in 1645 after one of his spiritual advisers, Konchog Chophel (d. 1646), pointed out that the site was ideal as a seat of government, situated as it is between Drepung and Sera monasteries and the old city of Lhasa. The Dalai Lama and his government moved into the Potrang Karpo ('White Palace') in 1649. Construction lasted until 1694, some twelve years after his death. The Potala was used as a winter palace by the Dalai Lama from that time. The Potrang Marpo ('Red Palace') was added between 1690 and 1694.
strategy: Palace of Potal requires Buddhism and it increases gold and culture in all cities with State religion and reduces War Weariness in all cities. It also increases wealth, science, culture and food output in the city where it's built.

name: Potter
pedia: The invention of pottery was essential to the development of agricultural societies. To get the most out of seasonal crops and domesticated animals, a tribe needed sturdy, waterproof containers in which to store and protect surplus food. The discovery of the properties of clay, and the invention of the kiln and the potter's wheel made it possible to build such containers. The earliest examples of Western pottery date back to as early as 6500 BC. Most of the examples from this period were strictly utilitarian. Although use continued to be primarily practical, decorative pottery soon became a ritualistic and aesthetic art form in cultures all over the world. Some of the most impressive examples of artistic pottery comes from the pre-Columbian cultures of South America, and from the Ming dynasty in 14th century China.
strategy: Provides Pottery

name: Power Receiver
pedia: Broadcast power has a long history of scientific interest and development, dating back to Nikola Tesla. The power receiver is the large-scale application of the perfected concept. This tower is capable of receiving enough electricity to power an entire city, beamed from a fusion power plant.
strategy: The {color:building_text}Power Receiver{/color} provides clean power to a city. It requires a {color:building_text}Fusion Power Plant{/color} to build.

name: Press Agency
pedia: A press agency is an organization of journalists established to supply news reports to organizations in the news trade: newspapers, magazines, and radio and television broadcasters. Such an agency may also be referred to as a news agency, wire service, newswire or news service.[PARAGRAPH:]The oldest news agency is Agence France-Presse (AFP). It was founded in 1835 by a Parisian translator and advertising agent, Charles-Louis Havas as Agence Havas. Two of his employees, Paul Julius Reuter and Bernhard Wolff, later set up rival news agencies in London and Berlin respectively.
